Subject: Order Form — Exhibit mapping + rollback path

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this on. We've reviewed the draft Exhibit C you sent last week and we have two items that need explicit language before procurement will approve the change order: 1) a clear rollback trigger and mechanism if the SOW change causes integration regressions during the first 30 days, and 2) confirmation about billing proration for partial-month capacity adds.

I'm attaching our annotated SOW (alt_health_sow_v3.pdf) and a small spreadsheet with the procurement-specific acceptance gates (redlines.xlsx).

Can your legal team propose amendment language that contains: a 30-day rollback window, an ops handback clause (how we fall back to the previous Exhibit), and a short acceptance checklist? Also — because our FY-end is on Aug 31 — if we sign a change that goes live mid-August, procurement wants a billing credit for the unused portion rather than pro-rating the full month.

Elena Cruz
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
AltHealth Solutions

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the annotated files. Quick summary of the approach we recommend:

- Create a narrow Change Order (Amendment A-1) that only alters Exhibit C and appends a 30-day "trial" acceptance period.
- Add a rollback clause: if AltHealth reports a regression tied to the Exhibit changes within 30 days and provides logs and a reproducible test case, Redwood will revert the Exhibit to the prior version and issue a service credit for the impacted period.
- Billing: Redwood proposes a credit model instead of retroactive proration — we can credit the unused portion if the change is rolled back, or offer a one-time onboarding credit if the change is accepted mid-billing cycle.

I've attached a short proposed patch (proposed_patch_exhibitC.docx) that captures the language for legal to review. Next steps: Laura, can you take a first pass on the rollback wording and the acceptance checklist? Karthik — I'll need a recommended credit band we can offer to procurement (small % or flat $) so they can accept quickly.

Target dates: draft legal language by Thu 8/6; procurement sign-off target Fri 8/13 to meet AltHealth timeline.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson

Hi all —

Thanks for looping me in, Avery. I reviewed the proposed patch and AltHealth's annotations. High-level legal notes:

1) Rollback trigger: we should limit to regressions "materially caused by the Exhibit changes and reproducible by AltHealth with Redwood's logs". We'll require a 5-business-day triage window for remediation before a rollback is executed, and Redwood retains the right to propose a hotfix.

2) Acceptance checklist: include 5 items (smoke test pass, integration throughput within 10% of baseline, KV cache integrity check, endpoint auth validation, and documentation handoff). Each item requires a named AltHealth approver.

3) Billing/credits: legal is comfortable with a credit approach but we need to cap exposure. Recommend: credit equals monthly fee for the affected feature prorated to full days impacted, capped at 25% of the monthly invoice for the affected SKU. That gives procurement certainty while protecting Redwood against open-ended liability.

4) Execution flow: amendment executed via DocuSign; amendment references the MSA and Order Form by amendment number and effective timestamp; include an ops contact for rollback requests.

I've attached a redline extract and suggested legal text (see excerpt below). If AltHealth accepts the cap + 5-business-day triage window, we should be able to finalize fast.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--

We attached procurement_requirements.docx with the suggested edits. For timeline: procurement is pushing for execution the week of Aug 9 so we can onboard before our FY-end; they will escalate to VP procurement if we need extra credit latitude.

Would Redwood consider a compromise: 15% cap for the first 60 days of the pilot, then revert to 25% going forward? That would satisfy procurement and limit Redwood's exposure over time.

Elena — quick response from my side on credit/pricing:

- We can agree to the staged cap: 15% for the first 60 days, then 25% thereafter. That is acceptable commercially for a pilot and lines up with our standard exposure limits.
- Regarding rollback without hotfix: we can add a clause that allows AltHealth to request an immediate rollback if a regression "materially degrades production SLA performance"; Redwood will still have a 5-business-day window to propose a hotfix, but acceptance of rollback will be available if the impact is severe and documented.
- Billing proration: we'll follow the credit model (no retroactive prorate beyond the credit applied). If AltHealth prefers an upfront onboarding credit instead of a rollback credit, we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first-month fee in lieu of credits for rollback.

Next steps: Laura to publish final amendment language today; Avery to send DocuSign package with the amendment + SOW patch. Can we target DocuSign send on Thu 8/6 and sign-off by Fri 8/13? If procurement needs earlier, we can accelerate.

I'll note the commercial concession in the HubSpot deal (see link).
